chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim told me from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: A group of our companions told me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The proficient (suitable match) is the one who is chaste and who has solvency (financial means).

key_terms.الْكُفُؤُ: Suitable match or proficient spouse, equal in status
key_terms.يَسَارٌ: Solvency, financial means, or ease in provision

ai.seo_question: What are the primary conditions for a suitable match (kufu') in Shia Islamic marriage jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that *kufu'* (suitability) in marriage requires both moral purity (*iffah*) and financial capacity (*ysar*). This definition reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on balancing spiritual integrity with practical ability to maintain a household, distinguishing it from mere tribal lineage or wealth alone. The hadith underscores that a suitable match must be capable of fulfilling marital obligations through both character and resources.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, that he said: I was told by Ibrahim bin Hashim, from Isma’eel bin Marrar, from Yunus bin Abdul-Rahman, that he said: I was told by a group of our companions, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
The proficient is the one who is chaste and who has solvency.
